Learnings:
- Feed is extremely wide (16 components, b.p. 185-424K). No single column can create a 95%-pure or blend-qualifying stream; every split leaves both T and B impure, so revenue stays $0 while column cost is positive -> negative reward.
- Converging difficulty: high-reflux/large-stage columns (100 stages R=3 with side draw; 120 stages) FAILED to converge. My 90/1.2/1.2 and 70/4.0/4.0 (agent-3) converged but gave -0.27 to -0.56. Sharper/hotter columns are prone to non-convergence, and NON-CONVERGENCE invalidates the whole plant.
- Blends (C4mix, C5mix, C6 paraffin mix) are worth $100s M/yr at 95% member purity, far above column cost, so a multi-column tree targeting them is theoretically the winner — but it needs ~3-4 columns to converge, which I never achieved within budget (with side draws especially).
- Strategy lesson: should have budgeted solves for incremental single-column tuning rather than a 3-column tree built in one call. Getting a converged base first, then adding one column at a time, is the winning approach for next time.
